messages:
maya: Heads-up — planning to publish py and ts SDKs in the 18:00 UTC change window. Need final signoff on the docs and version pins.

oliver: +1 on timing. Are we still publishing py 2.1.0 and ts 3.4.0 together?

maya: yes. py 2.1.0 contains the async client split; ts 3.4.0 has the new streaming helpers. Both require changelog entries and a short migration note.

sasha: Docs: I pushed most of the migration snippets to the site branch, but the code sample for conversational streaming needs one more tweak (token handling). I can finish by 17:20 UTC.

maya: perfect. jen, can you confirm packaging and CI? any flaky tests we should worry about?

jen: CI green on main now. There is one intermittent test in test_streaming.py — I marked as flaky and added retry. Packaging: wheel build works, I verified `python -m build` locally. npm pack + publish dry-run succeeds.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot posted: release-checklist passed for py@2.1.0, ts@3.4.0 — all required CI jobs succeeded.

oliver: rollback plan? If we need to revert quickly, what's the fastest path for each registry?

release-manager: plan outlined:
- npm: `npm deprecate @redwood/sdk@3.4.0 "broken"` then republish fixed patch 3.4.1 and update tags.
- pypi: delete the release is not allowed; instead publish 2.1.1 with a clear post-release note and pin server-side compat check to ignore 2.1.0. Also push a rollback tag `v2.1.0-reverted` to the repo for traceability.
- For both: update the redwood SDK routing in the console to fallback to hosted-compat v3.3.x if health probes show regressions.

maya: good. Also let's add a temporary client feature flag to the runtime routing so we can toggle new streaming by customer if needed. eng-runtime can enable fallback within 5m after a rollback request.

jen: FYI publishing commands I will run in the window (after changelog approved):
```
# python
python -m build && twine upload dist/*
# npm
npm publish --access public
```

sasha: docs checklist: changelog, migration snippet, example gist, and a short note in the SDK readme. All PRs linked in the release PR. I will request a docs-review from oliver at 17:25.

oliver: I'll do a quick pass. If anything major, call hold. Otherwise I approve the release notes and migration steps.

maya: final decision: proceed with publish at 18:00 UTC. If oliver raises a hold before 17:40, we delay to the next window.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot posted: scheduled release job for 1768605600 (18:00 UTC) queued.

release-manager: tagging policy reminder: create annotated git tags `v2.1.0` and `v3.4.0` from main after merge, include SHA in release notes, and attach built artifacts to the GitHub release.

jen: I'll be on the release channel during the window. Contact me if any publish step fails; I can run the deprecate + republish flow.

maya: thanks team. Post-publish, let's monitor error rates for 30m and roll if we see >2% 5m error spike for clients using streaming.

sasha: docs PR merged at 17:39 UTC. migration snippets updated.

oliver: approved at 17:41 UTC — proceeding.

maya: publishing now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot posted: release job started for py@2.1.0, ts@3.4.0.

jen: py uploaded to pypi, npm publish completed. Artifacts attached.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot posted: smoke checks passed. No immediate regressions.

maya: monitoring… so far so good.

release-manager: note for audit — added release notes link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/releases/tag/v2.1.0 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/releases/tag/v3.4.0

jen: small follow-up: found a minor usage edge where streaming with long prefixes consumes more memory in older runtimes. Filed internal ticket INF-1427 and will ship a 2.1.1 patch if it reproduces in customer traffic.

maya: adding INF-1427 to post-release action items. Thanks everyone :shipit:
